Distribution. Only known from the type locality in Central Sulawesi, Indonesia (Fig. 3).

Distribution and ecology. The new species is currently only known from Tuoniang River Basin (upper reach of the You River) in Yunnan and Guangxi, a sub-basin in the upper Pearl River system (Fig. 3). Molecular phylogeny Both phylogenetic methods (ML and BI) recovered a similar tree in topology (Fig. 4), based on two mitochondrial gene fragments (Cyt b, CO I) and also consistent with the results reported by Jiang et al. (2011). Species with dark brown to dark yellow body and black saddle-like patches beneath the dorsal and adipose fin formed a distinct monophyletic clade (in green), represented by Glyptothorax hainanensis, G. honghensis and G. sinensis. Species with a dark body and creamy or bright yellow spots or stripes formed another distinct monophyletic clade (in orange), represented by Glyptothorax pulcher sp. nov., G. quadriocellatus and G. pallozonum. The monophyly of the new species is strongly supported. Phylogenetic evidence indicated that G. pulcher is closely related to G. pallozonum, both of which are from the Pearl River, the estimated K 2 P genetic distances between the two range from 5.7 % to 6.0 % (Table 3).
